body: The current Test captain’s response to the fresh allegations comes as David Warner said he supported Bancroft’s 4,000-word account of the tour of South Africa, which the former Australia player said he wrote after Cummins denied all knowledge of sandpaper being taken on to the field in Cape Town eight years ago.

articles.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
articles.summary: It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again. In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the…
body: Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

In the six years after being crowned kings of Europe, United turned to Wilf McGuinness, Busby stepped in temporarily to keep them up, then Frank O’Farrell was appointed before they landed on Tommy Docherty, who experienced the ignominy of taking them down.
In the past eight years, United have sacked José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and now Michael Carrick.

How did the United of 1974 go down? Most outsiders believed they were too big to fail. Inside the club, though, they sensed the direction of travel. After a heavy defeat at Crystal Palace in December 1972, Busby offered Docherty the job in the Selhurst Park boardroom. “There’s a lot of trouble in the camp,” Busby said. Docherty was doing well as Scotland manager and took a few days to mull it over, but decided he couldn’t turn down the opportunity.

“She is a top, young talent and is so mature on and off the pitch,” said Sonia Bompastor. “She is a confident player and a really complete player.”

Bompastor’s side were frustrated by Häcken last week, held to a 0-0 draw by the Swedish side and falling out of the top four automatic qualification places. There was a desire to put things right at AFC Wimbledon’s stadium and they did just that, albeit in not the prettiest of encounters.
“Sometimes in football you need to find a way to win and the result tonight was really important for us,” said Bompastor.

articles.title: MLB commissioner Manfred cites fan support for salary cap as baseball heads towards lockout
articles.summary: 2027 season under threat amid dispute over salary cap. Commissioner says fans want a more equal game. MLB commissioner, Rob Manfred, has insisted owners will not budge from their demand for a salary cap, leaving the league on track for a lockout starting 2 December that could threaten the 2027…
body: “I can’t imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor,” Manfred said on Wednesday at a news conference during an owners meeting. Players say they will never accept a cap. The last time management proposed a cap in 1994, it led to a strike that lasted almost eight months and caused the cancellation of the World Series for the first time in 90 years.

“There’s plenty of room for compromise, but there’s one thing that I will not compromise and that’s the issue that we’re hearing from the vast majority of our fans: They want a salary cap and floor and on that we will not compromise,” Manfred continued. “We are not prepared to tell 70% of our fans that they’re wrong on this issue. Competitive balance is a serious problem, and it needs to be addressed and it’s one that we can’t avoid just because the negotiation may be difficult.”

Baseball’s five-year collective bargaining agreement expires at 11.59pm EST on 1 December. A lockout, which would be the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972, would bring to a halt all trades and signings.

articles.title: Missouri Basketball Dominates to Bounce Back With 61 Point Victory
articles.summary: Missouri delivered one of its most dominant performances of the young season on Wednesday night, crushing Alcorn State 102-41 at Mizzou Arena. The Tigers controlled the game from the opening minutes, overwhelmed the Braves on both ends of the floor and secured a convincing 61 point victory.
body: The win moves Missouri to 4-1 on the season and gives head coach Dennis Gates’ team another opportunity to build momentum after its recent victory over Marquette. The Tigers also welcomed back an important contributor, as Mark Mitchell returned to the lineup after missing the previous game with a concussion.

The Tigers wasted little time establishing their dominance. Missouri opened the game with strong offensive execution, consistently finding opportunities around the basket while making life difficult for Alcorn State defensively.

The Braves struggled to find any rhythm, shooting poorly from the field and having difficulty dealing with Missouri’s size and athleticism. The Tigers took advantage of those struggles, creating separation through defensive stops, rebounds and transition opportunities.
Missouri carried a commanding 51-18 advantage into halftime. The 33 point lead reflected just how one-sided the opening 20 minutes had become.

articles.title: Van Gerwen: I need my A-game to beat Wade at Grand Slam
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen believes James Wade is "in some of the best form of his life" and says he'll need to bring his "A-game" in order to win their second-round meeting at the Grand Slam of Darts.
body: Their clash on Thursday night - live on Sky Sports+ and Main Event from 7pm - is a rematch of the 2016 final, in which Van Gerwen claimed the second of his three consecutive titles.
But it's Wade, a three-time runner-up at the event, who is the form player of the pair leading into the last 16 matchup, having dropped only one leg across his two group-stage wins.

Van Gerwen, contrastingly, saw both his wins over Henry Coates and Jeffrey de Graaf come down to last-leg deciders. He averaged 100 against Coates, but that dropped to 90 against De Graaf, a match in which he missed seven match darts.
"It wasn't a good game at all," Van Gerwen, seeded 10th at the tournament, told Sky Sports after his victory over De Graaf.

articles.title: Wattimena wins hearts with win vs Littler: 'Beat him, the crowd loves you'
articles.summary: Jermaine Wattimena was visibly emotional following his massive 10-8 win over Luke Littler in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts, taking in the moment as the Wolverhampton crowd sang his name.
body: An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over.
Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat.
Wattimena led 3-2 before running away to get 7-2 up against Littler. He then held on as Littler fought back to 9-8 and pinned 77 on tops for what is now the biggest win of his career.
It was made all the sweeter given the fact Wattimena has felt the pain of a massive Littler comeback before. He was 7-2 up against 'The Nuke' at the Matchplay in 2025 before eventually being beaten.

articles.title: Littler stunned by Wattimena at Grand Slam of Darts
articles.summary: Luke Littler's title defence at the Grand Slam of Darts is over after he suffered a 10-8 loss to Jermaine Wattimena in the last 16 in Wolverhampton.
body: It was simply a stunning performance from Wattimena in which he averaged 101.7, outscoring the world No 1 and outplaying him in every facet, hitting 10 180s and 11 140s on the way.
The loss for Littler means he will not join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen on a short but illustrious list of players who have won the Grand Slam three times in a row.

Littler had picked up the Grand Slam title in 2024 with a win over Martin Lukeman and then backed that up with victory over Luke Humphries in 2025. But his attempt at a hat-trick was shattered with Wattimena's win blowing the competition wide open.
"It feels emotional, absolutely incredible," Wattimena told Sky Sports immediately after the victory.

articles.title: Ukrainian FA to blame for failed drugs test - Mudryk
articles.summary: Tottenham's on-loan Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk says he blames the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban.
body: The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, which he believes entered his system while on international duty.
Having initially faced a four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport was successful.
He returned to football after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension equivalent to the time he had already served.
After appearing for Chelsea during a pre-season tour of Asia, Mudryk joined Tottenham on transfer deadline day to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto de Zerbi.

articles.title: FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on
articles.summary: The Football Association considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, but it felt a case was likely to fail.
body: The Football Association has considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, BBC Sport can reveal.
But it believes any attempt to prevent him from standing in the election in March is likely to fail.
The FA has also confirmed it is backing rival candidate Philippe Diallo.
Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter as leader of world football's governing body.
